_comment: DELTA's brain: localization, depth, and the map it builds for itself.
Ported from the Spatial Memory Glasses project (spatial-agent-12), whose
settings these are. Every number here was tuned there against Habitat's
navmesh, so they are measurements rather than guesses -- except the ones
under `drone`, which are this robot's own.
Sections the glasses had and DELTA does not: detection (YOLOE), objects
(object memory), hazard (the blind-wearer beeps), guidance, speech and
language (Piper and Gemma). DELTA maps; it does not talk to anybody.

_frame_rate: Stereo pairs per second from the sim. Odometry sees every one; depth,
detection and the hazard loop each take the newest when they are free.

localization._keyframe_every: seconds between frames offered to RTAB-Map's map; odometry sees all
_parameters: Force3DoF: a walking person stays level, so x, y and heading only.
OptimizeFromGraphEnd false: the oldest node stays put when a loop
closes, so a map saved last session keeps its coordinates.
InitWMWithAllNodes: every remembered place is a candidate for
recognising where we are, not just the most recent ones.
localization._relocalize_within: seconds to recognise last session's map before starting a new one

_comment: How far a loop closure may move the drone before it is taken for a
lookalike -- a place that merely resembles one already mapped -- and
thrown out. Allowed = 0.5 m + jump_per_metre x metres travelled +
jump_per_lost_frame x frames tracking was lost, all since the last
trusted closure.
jump_per_metre 0.02: RTAB-Map drifts about 1% here (0.33 m over 31 m,
0.59 m over 58 m, tests/scripts/baseline.json and diagnose.json), so
twice that. The glasses used 0.05.
jump_per_lost_frame 0.10: the drone's top speed of 0.8 m/s for one
0.1 s frame is 0.08 m, plus margin. The glasses used 0.25, sized to a
person walking blind, and after 18 lost frames that let a 3.5 m false
closure through.

_scale_from_floor: DA3 two-view read ~12% short in #11. The floor is the fix: the lens
height above it is known, so the distance DA3 reports to it gives the
missing scale on every frame. Uncorrected, the floor would sit 20 cm
up and every frame would mark it as an obstacle.

_obstacle_band: Heights above the floor that stop a ROLLING drone: from its climb limit
(0.08 m, project.json max_climb) to a little over its own height (0.30 m
plus 8 cm). This grid is the rolling map -- it answers 'can the drone
roll here' -- and it is scored against the drone's navmesh, which asks
It was the glasses' 0.15-1.9 m, sized to hit a standing adult, with the
note 'lamps and ceilings are above it'. In this house they are not: the
ceiling is about 1.97 m, 7 cm above the cut-off. A camera 15 cm off the
floor looking up at 47 degrees sees ceiling for metres around it, and a
few cm of tilt or lens-height error dragged those points under 1.9 m,
where they were stamped onto the empty floor below. Measured: with
PERFECT pose and depth, 32.7% of clear floor was marked solid, and 98%
of those cells had nothing above them but a ceiling at 1.95-2.05 m
(tools/explain_phantoms.py). Overhead things -- table tops, lamps, the
ceiling -- are the 2.5D map's job, not this one's.
_evidence: An obstacle needs about three sightings; one clear view of the floor
clears a cell. Tuned on a recorded walk against Habitat's navmesh: the
first guess (one hit marked a cell, hit 0.85, threshold 0.7) left 6.2%
phantom obstacles in walkable space and 8 of 21 test routes
occupancy._keyframe_spacing: metres and degrees of movement before another view is kept for redrawing the map

_comment: Is this cell under cover? Log-odds, exactly like the occupancy
evidence beside it, and for the same reason: one glimpse of a
doorframe must not turn a garden into a room, and driving out
through a door has to be able to change the answer back.
Weaker than the occupancy evidence on purpose. A missed obstacle
is a collision; a cell wrongly called indoors is a label on a map.
So it needs two or three agreeing views either way to commit.

_autosave_seconds: How often the map is written to disk while running. It used to be saved
only when the sim disconnected, so anything that killed the process lost

_comment: Replaces the glasses' `wearer`. The numbers are the drone's, and two
of the three are different in kind, not just in value:
lens_height  the cameras sit at the CENTRE of the sphere, so this is
its radius -- 0.15 m, not a standing adult's 1.741 m.
Depth uses it to fix Depth Anything's scale, so getting
it wrong scales every distance in the map.
radius       half the drone, for inflating the map when planning.
lens_forward is gone. For the glasses it was head radius plus visor:
how far in front of the body the lenses sit. A sphere's
centre IS the lens position, so the offset is zero and
the term would only add error.
While the drone flies, the sim sends its altitude each frame and the
brain adds it to lens_height -- otherwise every height in the map
would shift down by however high the drone had climbed.
